meta.description: An anonymous multilingual infrastructure engineering case study covering Linux hosting, mail services, secure remote access, MikroTik networking and hybrid connectivity.

hero.label: Sanitized Portfolio Case Study
hero.title: Hybrid Corporate Web and Mail Infrastructure
hero.lead: An anonymous engineering case study covering website delivery, Linux hosting, enterprise mail services, secure remote access and hybrid network integration.

overview.title: A unified web, mail and network operations case study
overview.body: This portfolio describes a sanitized infrastructure project that brought together a corporate website, Linux-based hosting, managed mail services, reverse proxying, secure external access, routed internal access, DNS authentication, backup planning and operational troubleshooting.

challenge.title: Balancing public delivery, internal reliability and mail control
challenge.body: The organization needed a maintainable platform for website delivery and corporate email while supporting different access paths for internal and external users. The architecture also needed practical security controls, reliable DNS and email authentication, and recovery procedures that could be used during incidents.

role.title: Milad owned the integration work across web, Linux, mail and network layers
role.body: Milad designed and implemented the website presentation layer, deployed and administered the hosting environment, configured mail services, integrated secure connectivity, coordinated DNS authentication and maintained troubleshooting documentation. The work focused on installing, configuring, integrating, securing and operating established technologies.

implemented.title: Practical work delivered across the platform
implemented.body: The public case study describes completed implementation and administration responsibilities, not a theoretical proposal. Exact production values are intentionally omitted.

architecture.title: Generalized hybrid architecture
architecture.body: The public portfolio diagram intentionally removes provider names, addresses, hostnames, interface names and exact routing values. It shows only the engineering responsibilities and the relationship between major components.

decisions.title: Why the platform was shaped this way
decisions.body: The implementation favored maintainable operational boundaries: public access through controlled edges, mail authentication through DNS records, internal access through routed paths, and public documentation through sanitized abstractions.

web.title: Website delivery and Linux hosting administration
web.body: The case study covers website design and implementation, deployment to a Linux hosting environment, HestiaCP administration, Nginx hosting, reverse proxy behavior, TLS management and practical maintenance routines.

mail.title: Corporate email services with controlled delivery paths
mail.body: Mail operations included Exim SMTP, Dovecot IMAP, Roundcube webmail, TLS access, internal and external mailbox access, relay integration and domain-based outbound mail routing concepts.

connectivity.title: Secure external entry and internal routed access
connectivity.body: A European VPS provided a controlled external entry point. HAProxy and SMTP relay behavior were integrated with an encrypted WireGuard path toward the internal edge router, where firewall, NAT and policy-based routing decisions were maintained at a high level.

routing.title: Controlled paths for users, domains and services
routing.body: Routing was documented as a set of responsibilities rather than public configuration. The portfolio distinguishes internal access, external access, reverse proxy behavior, relay behavior and domain-specific outbound mail handling.

security.title: Sanitized security approach
security.body: Security work focused on TLS, firewall rules, NAT boundaries, authentication records, reduced exposure, credential hygiene, backup separation and public documentation that never exposes production values.

recovery.title: Troubleshooting, incident recovery and validation
recovery.body: The recovery story is documented as a generalized operational process: symptoms, investigation, root cause category, restoration, validation and preventive documentation. It avoids real logs, command history, hostnames or incident identifiers.

validation.title: Checks used before publishing and after changes
validation.body: The repository includes local and CI-friendly checks for locale consistency, JavaScript syntax, required files, internal links, HTML structure, CSS guardrails and privacy-sensitive content.

outcomes.title: Operational results represented in the portfolio
outcomes.body: The project outcome is presented as a privacy-safe professional record of implemented infrastructure work: web delivery, mail operations, network integration, security posture, documentation and recovery discipline.

stack.title: Technologies administered and integrated
stack.body: The portfolio names technologies as administered, configured and integrated components. It does not claim authorship of third-party software.

lessons.title: Operational lessons from hybrid infrastructure work

docs.title: Repository documentation
docs.body: Supporting Markdown files explain architecture, responsibilities, privacy scope, security posture, testing, recovery and maintenance without exposing production details.

outcomes: Centralized web and mail services under a maintainable operating model.
Enabled secure internal and external access without publishing production identifiers.
Established encrypted connectivity between infrastructure locations.
Created repeatable validation, backup and recovery documentation.

items.title: Public website delivery
items.body: The platform needed to serve a corporate website through a controlled hosting path with HTTPS and reverse proxy awareness.

items.title: Mail access patterns
items.body: Internal and external users needed reliable access to SMTP, IMAP and webmail without exposing unnecessary infrastructure detail.

items.title: Outbound routing control
items.body: Different hosted domains required direct and relayed outbound SMTP concepts while keeping DNS authentication aligned.

items.title: Website and hosting
items.body: Designed, deployed and maintained the website layer on a Linux hosting stack.

items.title: Mail services
items.body: Configured SMTP, IMAP and webmail services with TLS-aware access paths.

items.title: Network integration
items.body: Integrated public entry, internal routing and encrypted transport concepts.

items.title: Operations
items.body: Documented validation, recovery and privacy-safe portfolio review routines.

items: Use established services instead of custom mail or routing software.
Keep public web delivery, mail transport and internal access responsibilities distinct.
Document concepts without exposing hostnames, addresses, mailbox data or secrets.
Validate changes with repeatable checks before treating the system as healthy.

items.title: Static and dynamic delivery
items.body: Implemented and deployed the website layer while keeping the portfolio separate from production source.

items.title: Hosting administration
items.body: Configured HestiaCP and Nginx hosting behavior, TLS certificates and operational maintenance routines.

items.title: Reverse proxy integration
items.body: Integrated a generalized reverse proxy path so public access could be routed through a controlled edge.

items.title: Health checks
items.body: Used practical validation steps after hosting, TLS, routing or filesystem changes.

flow: Inbound mail was coordinated through public DNS, MX concepts and a Linux-based mail server.
Exim handled SMTP submission and transport while Dovecot provided IMAP mailbox access.
Roundcube provided browser-based webmail for users who needed a managed web interface.
Outbound mail could use direct or relayed paths depending on the hosted domain policy.
SPF, DKIM, DMARC, MX and PTR concepts were documented as part of deliverability and trust.

items.title: External entry point
items.body: A European VPS acted as a sanitized public edge for selected access paths.

items.title: Encrypted tunnel
items.body: WireGuard provided a secure site-to-site transport concept between infrastructure locations.

items.title: Edge routing
items.body: MikroTik RouterOS handled firewall, NAT and policy-based routing responsibilities.

items.title: Service relay
items.body: HAProxy and SMTP relay behavior supported controlled external access and outbound delivery.

flow: Internal users reached services through routed internal paths.
External users reached selected services through a controlled public edge.
Reverse proxy behavior separated public entry from backend service placement.
Domain policy determined whether outbound SMTP used direct or relayed delivery.
DNS records supported mail trust while avoiding disclosure of production values.

items: No production identifiers are published in this repository.
TLS, DNS authentication and access boundaries are described at a high level.
Credentials, keys, backups, mailbox data and configuration exports are excluded.
Privacy scanners are included to catch prohibited names, addresses and secret patterns.
The documentation is a portfolio narrative, not deployment guidance.

timeline: Symptoms were documented from user-visible behavior and service health checks.
Investigation separated website files, control panel files, mail services and routing layers.
Root cause category: hosting control panel application dependencies became unavailable after a filesystem-related change.
Recovery focused on restoring required application files, validating services and avoiding unrelated changes.
Preventive actions emphasized backup verification, path validation and clearer recovery notes.

items: Locale files must share the same structure across English, German, Persian and Arabic.
Public links are checked so GitHub Pages does not ship broken local paths.
Privacy scanners reject production names, addresses, secrets and risky configuration patterns.
GitHub Pages deployment stages only the public site assets into the artifact.

items.title: Maintainable operations
items.body: Responsibilities were documented in a way another operator could follow conceptually.

items.title: Secure public narrative
items.body: The public repository tells the engineering story without exposing the real environment.

items.title: Multilingual presentation
items.body: The project can be reviewed in English, German, Persian and Arabic.

items.title: Automated hygiene
items.body: Validation scripts and workflows reduce accidental publishing mistakes.

items: Separate production configuration from public documentation.
Test restore procedures, not only backup creation.
Treat control panel files separately from hosted website files.
Validate filesystem paths before destructive operations.
Keep network and mail routing documentation current.
Use explicit health checks after infrastructure changes.
Protect keys and credentials from version control.
Use staged changes for critical mail systems.
Verify DNS, TLS and routing together.
